$comment: CQR setup manifest — consumed by cais-shared-services/scripts/setup-product-credentials.mjs. Schema is portfolio-canonical; see cais-shared-services/scripts/setup-manifest.example.json for the reference. CQR fills values, does not customise structure (per Rule 6, anti-fork).
$note_on_slack_discord: Slack bot tokens (xoxb-) and Discord bot tokens are NOT in this manifest — they're captured per-workspace via /setup/slack and /setup/discord after deploy. The operator can run CQR with zero messaging providers connected (just the dashboard) and add workspaces later. This manifest covers everything CQR needs at deploy time.

credentials.description: Your Supabase project URL (create the project at https://supabase.com/dashboard/projects). The wizard pushes the CQR migration suite to this DB.
Anon key — Settings → API in your Supabase dashboard. Public, safe for client-side use.
Service role key — Settings → API. Server-only, bypasses RLS. Treat as password.
Claude API key — Haiku for classification, Sonnet for drafting. Either this OR OPENROUTER_API_KEY is required.
Alternative to Anthropic — routes through OpenRouter (multi-provider, often cheaper).
Email sending for Supabase Auth magic links + (optional) draft-ready notifications.
Verified sender (e.g. noreply@yourdomain.com). Must be verified in Resend before magic-link login works.
Voice AI agent for operator-capture-a-learning (per VOICE AI STANDARD RULE — voice surface is non-negotiable in BYOK-free releases).
Created automatically below — leave blank unless you have a specific agent ID. The wizard's post-action writes the new agent_id back into the system_config Supabase table, not into env vars.
Random string protecting /api/cron/* endpoints. Generate any 32+ char random value.
Your deployed app URL (e.g. https://yourapp.vercel.app, or http://localhost:3000 for dev). Used as the OpenRouter HTTP-Referer header + magic-link redirect base.

config.name: CQR Operator Agent
config.system_prompt: You are the Community Question Responder operator's voice assistant. Help the operator capture learnings, review drafts, and discuss community-reply strategy. Match the operator's opinionated-practitioner voice. Keep replies under three sentences unless asked for depth. When the operator describes a learning (an API gotcha, a workaround, a real-world bug), summarise it back in one tight sentence, ask what vendor/namespace it belongs to, and confirm before you would ingest. Do not invent vendor names — if the operator doesn't specify one, ask.
config.first_message: Hey, what did you just learn? Tell me and I'll get it into the knowledge base.
